summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted with a four-day history of non-bloody diarrhea, vomiting, and headache. He was dehydrated on presentation and treated with IV fluids. Stool studies for C. difficile, Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, and E. coli O157:H7 were negative, supporting a diagnosis of noninfectious enteritis. A CT scan performed for liver follow-up showed stable findings post-TACE and RFA, with no new enhancing lesions. Colonic wall thickening was noted but attributed to portal hypertension. His symptoms improved during the hospital stay, and he was discharged home with continued management of his chronic liver disease and HCC. Diuretics were held initially but resumed on discharge, and all other baseline medications were continued.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis
